```plato
//==
// # Transform interfaces
//
// The interfaces that mark a value as carryable through a transform:
// ITransformable2D/3D for the general transform of a dimension, IDeformable2D/3D
// for an arbitrary point mapping. Deformable inherits Transformable — an
// arbitrary point mapping subsumes any named transform — so implementing Deform
// is the only obligation a shape has, and Transform arrives derived.
// Also the interfaces that mark a transform representation by the canonical form
// it converts into: IAffine2D/IAffine3D for the general affine transform of a
// dimension, IRotational3D for the unit quaternion.
// A transform maps points to points. The representations themselves are declared
// in the `transforms-*.plato` files (pose, TRS, affine/projective, frames,
// motor) and their operations in the matching `transforms-*.library.plato`
// files; the derived bodies for the interfaces below live in
// `intervals.library.plato` and
// `intervals-transforms-deformable.library.plato`. The shared conventions of
// the whole transform surface are stated once here.

//==
// # Transform operations
//
// Conversions between every transform representation, application to points and
// vectors (`p.Transform(t)`), composition, inverses, and identity statics.
//
// Conventions used throughout:
// - Matrices are row-vector style (v * M), matching System.Numerics: the product
//   a.Multiply(b) applies a first, then b.
// - Quaternion Multiply is the Hamilton product (a.Multiply(b) applies b first);
//   Concatenate(a, b) applies a first, then b. Rotors and motors follow the
//   quaternion convention through their isomorphisms.
// - Compose(first, second) means "apply first, then second" on EVERY type, so
//   users never need to remember which product order a representation uses.
// - A function named after a type is an implicit conversion and must be
//   faithful (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Conversions). Each one here is
//   total on its stated precondition (e.g. Pose3D(Matrix4x4) requires a rigid
//   matrix).
// - EulerAngles: Yaw is about Y, Pitch about X, Roll about Z; RotationOrder
//   lists the axes in application order (first-applied first), about fixed
//   world axes.

// Can be carried through any transform of the plane, yielding a new Self.
// Transform2D is the widest 2D map (`transforms.types.plato`), so every other
// representation reaches this one member by converting up to it.
interface ITransformable2D
{
    Transform(x: Self, transform: Transform2D): Self;
}
```
